title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 104 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 542–545 (Night 104, continuing directly from nights-103), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 104 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Ḍawʾ al-Makān finds his wounded brother Sharrukān recovering and tells him of King Ḥardūb's death; the 'ascetic' at Sharrukān's side — Dhāt al-Dawāhī in disguise, Ḥardūb's daughter — hides her grief and vows revenge. That night, when the camp is asleep, she cuts off Sharrukān's head and kills his pages, slips past the vizier Dandān with a story of a saint she must follow, and vanishes. Dandān, unable to sleep, goes to Sharrukān's tent and finds the bodies; the army mourns, Dandān names the ascetic as the murderer, and Sharrukān is buried on the mountain. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-rābiʿatu baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fourth after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and fourth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ لَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَى أَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ وَجَدَهُ جَالِسًا وَالْعَابِدُ عِنْدَهُ فَفَرِحَ وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَنَّأَهُ بِالسَّلَامَةِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-malika ḍawʾa al-makāni lammā dakhala ʿalā akhīhi sharrukāna wajadahu jālisan wa-al-ʿābidu ʿindahu fa-fariḥa wa-aqbala ʿalayhi wa-hannaʾahu bi-al-salāmati
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that King Ḍawʾ al-Makān, when he entered upon his brother Sharrukān, found him sitting, and the worshipper beside him; and he rejoiced, and turned toward him, and congratulated him on the safety.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when King Ḍawʾ al-Makān went in to his brother Sharrukān, he found him sitting up, with the holy man beside him. He was glad, went to him, and wished him joy of his recovery.
sentences.n: The print has جانسا, a misprint for جالسا (jālisan, “sitting”), corrected here. السعيدان is the print’s run-together al-saʿīdu anna, kept as set, as in the last nights. The shadda on هنّأه is the print’s. “The worshipper” (al-ʿābid) is Dhāt al-Dawāhī, still disguised as an ascetic; hannaʾahu bi-al-salāma, “congratulated him on (bi-) his safety”, is the set phrase for welcoming someone back from danger or sickness.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ إِنَّنَا كُلَّنَا فِي بَرَكَةِ هَذَا الزَّاهِدِ وَمَا انْتَصَرْتُمْ إِلَّابِدُعَائِهِ لَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu innanā kullanā fī barakati hādhā al-zāhidi wa-mā intaṣartum illā bi-duʿāʾihi lakum
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: We, all of us, are in the blessing of this ascetic, and you did not conquer except by his praying for you.
sentences.i: Sharrukān said, “All of us live by the blessing of this holy man. You won only because he prayed for you.
sentences.n: إلابدعائه is printed as one word (illā bi-duʿāʾihi), and kept so.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ مَا بَرِحَ الْيَوْمَ وَهُوَ يَدْعُو لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu mā bariḥa al-yawma wa-huwa yadʿū li-al-muslimīna
sentences.l: For he did not leave-off today while he prays for the Muslims.
sentences.i: He has not stopped praying for the Muslims all day.
sentences.n: mā bariḥa, “he did not cease”, one of the verbs of continuing; here it is followed by a circumstantial clause (wa-huwa yadʿū) instead of the usual predicate.

sentences.t: وَكُنْتُ وَجَدْتُ فِي نَفْسِي قُوَّةً حِينَ سَمِعْتُ تَكْبِيرَكُمْ فَعَلِمْتُ أَنَّكُمْ مَنْصُورُونَ عَلَى أَعْدَائِكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-kuntu wajadtu fī nafsī quwwatan ḥīna samiʿtu takbīrakum fa-ʿalimtu annakum manṣūrūna ʿalā aʿdāʾikum
sentences.l: And I had found in myself a strength when I heard your takbīr, and I knew that you were made-victorious over your enemies.
sentences.i: I felt strength come into me when I heard you crying ‘God is most great’, and I knew you had been given victory over your enemies.
sentences.n: takbīr is the cry Allāhu akbar, “God is most great”, the Muslim battle-cry. manṣūr, “helped to victory”, is passive: the victory is God’s gift.

sentences.t: فَاحْكِ لِي يَا أَخِي مَا وَقَعَ لَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-iḥki lī yā akhī mā waqaʿa laka
sentences.l: So tell to me, O my brother, what befell you.
sentences.i: So tell me, my brother, what happened to you.”

sentences.t: فَحَكَى لَهُ جَمِيعَ مَا وَقَعَ لَهُ مَعَ الْمَلْعُونِ حَرْدُوبَ وَأَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهُ قَتَلَهُ وَرَاحَ إِلَى لَعْنَةِ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakā lahu jamīʿa mā waqaʿa lahu maʿa al-malʿūni ḥardūba wa-akhbarahu annahu qatalahu wa-rāḥa ilā laʿnati allāhi
sentences.l: And he told to him all that befell him with the accursed Ḥardūb, and informed him that he killed him and he went to the curse of God.
sentences.i: So he told him everything that had passed between him and the accursed Ḥardūb, and how he had killed him and Ḥardūb had gone to God’s curse.
sentences.n: rāḥa ilā laʿnati allāh, “he went to God’s curse”, is the tale’s set phrase for an enemy’s death.

sentences.t: فَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ وَشَكَرَ مَسْعَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-athnā ʿalayhi wa-shakara masʿāhu
sentences.l: And he praised him and thanked his striving.
sentences.i: Sharrukān praised him and thanked him for what he had done.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي وَهِيَ فِي صِفَةِ الزَّاهِدِ بِقَتْلِ وَالِدِهَا الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ انْقَلَبَ لَوْنُهَا بِالِاصْفِرَارِ وَتَغَرْغَرَتْ عَيْنَاهَا بِالدُّمُوعِ الْغِزَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat dhātu al-dawāhī wa-hiya fī ṣifati al-zāhidi bi-qatli wālidihā al-maliki ḥardūba inqalaba lawnuhā bi-al-iṣfirāri wa-taghargharat ʿaynāhā bi-al-dumūʿi al-ghizāri
sentences.l: And when Dhāt al-Dawāhī — and she in the guise of the ascetic — heard of the killing of her father, King Ḥardūb, her colour turned to the yellowing, and her two eyes brimmed with the abundant tears.
sentences.i: When Dhāt al-Dawāhī, still in the guise of the holy man, heard that her father King Ḥardūb had been killed, her face turned yellow and her eyes swam with heavy tears.
sentences.n: samiʿa bi-: “hear of, hear news of”. The rhyme falls on al-iṣfirār / al-ghizār. Ḥardūb is her father here, as earlier in the tale.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنَّهَا أَخْفَتْ ذَلِكَ وَأَظْهَرَتْ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ أَنَّهَا فَرِحَتْ وَأَنَّهَا تَبْكِي مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْفَرَحِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākinnahā akhfat dhālika wa-aẓharat li-al-muslimīna annahā fariḥat wa-annahā tabkī min shiddati al-faraḥi
sentences.l: But she hid that, and showed to the Muslims that she rejoiced and that she was weeping from the intensity of the joy.
sentences.i: But she hid it, and let the Muslims think she was glad and was weeping for sheer joy.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا قَالَتْ فِي نَفْسِهَا وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ مَابَقِيَ فِي حَيَاتِي فَائِدَةٌ إِنْ لَمْ أُحْرِقْ قَلْبَهُ عَلَى أَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ كَمَا أَحْرَقَ قَلْبِي عَلَى عِمَادِ الْمِلَّةِ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ وَالْعِصَابَةِ الصَّلِيبِيَّةِ الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā qālat fī nafsihā wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi mā baqiya fī ḥayātī fāʾidatun in lam uḥriq qalbahu ʿalā akhīhi sharrukāna kamā aḥraqa qalbī ʿalā ʿimādi al-millati al-naṣrāniyyati wa-al-ʿiṣābati al-ṣalībiyyati al-maliki ḥardūba
sentences.l: Then she said in herself: By the truth of the Messiah, there remains in my life no use, if I do not burn his heart over his brother Sharrukān as he burned my heart over the pillar of the Christian creed and the Cross-bearing band, King Ḥardūb.
sentences.i: Then she said to herself, “By the Messiah, my life is worth nothing if I do not burn his heart for his brother Sharrukān as he has burned mine for King Ḥardūb, pillar of the Christian faith and the company of the Cross.”
sentences.n: “His heart” is Ḍawʾ al-Makān’s: he killed Ḥardūb, and she means to kill his brother. مابقي is printed as one word (mā baqiya). wa-ḥaqqi, “by the truth of”, is an oath formula.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنَّهَا كَتَمَتْ مَا بِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lākinnahā katamat mā bihā
sentences.l: But she concealed what was in her.
sentences.i: But she kept what she felt to herself.
sentences.n: mā bihā, “what is with her”: her feelings, what afflicts her (bi-, “in, upon”).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ وَالْمَلِكَ شَرْكَانَ وَالْحَاجِبَ اسْتَمَرُّوا جَالِسِينَ عِنْدَ شَرْكَانَ حَتَّى عَمِلُوا لَهُ اللِّزَاقَ وَالْأَدْهَانَ وَأَعْطَوْهُ الدَّوَاءَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra dandāna wa-al-malika sharrukāna wa-al-ḥājiba istamarrū jālisīna ʿinda sharrukāna ḥattā ʿamilū lahu al-lizāqa wa-al-adhāna wa-aʿṭawhu al-dawāʾa
sentences.l: Then the vizier Dandān and King Sharrukān and the chamberlain continued sitting beside Sharrukān until they made for him the plaster and the ointments and gave him the medicine.
sentences.i: Then the vizier Dandān, the king and the chamberlain stayed sitting with Sharrukān until they had dressed his wound with plasters and ointments and given him his medicine.
sentences.n: The print names “King Sharrukān” among those sitting by Sharrukān. The king meant must be Ḍawʾ al-Makān; the slip is the text’s, kept as printed, and the idiomatic layer says only “the king”. al-lizāq: a sticking plaster or poultice laid on a wound.

sentences.t: فَتَوَجَّهَتْ إِلَيْهِ الْعَافِيَةُ وَفَرِحُوا بِذَلِكَ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا وَأَعْلَمُوا بِهِ الْعَسَاكِرَ
sentences.tr: fa-tawajjahat ilayhi al-ʿāfiyatu wa-fariḥū bi-dhālika faraḥan shadīdan wa-aʿlamū bihi al-ʿasākira
sentences.l: And the well-being turned toward him, and they rejoiced in that a strong rejoicing, and they informed of it the troops.
sentences.i: His health began to come back, and they were overjoyed and sent word of it to the troops.
sentences.n: aʿlama X bi-Y: “inform X of Y”; the bi- marks the news.

sentences.t: فَتَبَاشَرَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَقَالُوا فِي غَدٍ يَرْكَبُ مَعَنَا وَيُبَاشِرُ الْحِصَارَ
sentences.tr: fa-tabāshara al-muslimūna wa-qālū fī ghadin yarkabu maʿanā wa-yubāshiru al-ḥiṣāra
sentences.l: And the Muslims gave-each-other-good-tidings and said: In tomorrow he rides with us and takes-in-hand the siege.
sentences.i: The Muslims passed the good news among themselves and said, “Tomorrow he will ride with us and take charge of the siege.”
sentences.n: tabāshara, form VI, “give one another good news”, and yubāshiru, form III, “take something in hand”, are built on the same root (b-sh-r) and make a play of words.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ شَرْكَانَ قَالَ لَهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ قَاتَلْتُمُ الْيَوْمَ وَتَعِبْتُمْ مِنَ الْقِتَالِ فَيَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَتَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى أَمَاكِنِكُمْ وَتَنَامُوا وَلَا تَسْهَرُوا
sentences.tr: thumma inna sharrukāna qāla lahum innakum qātaltumu al-yawma wa-taʿibtum mina al-qitāli fa-yanbaghī an tatawajjahū ilā amākinikum wa-tanāmū wa-lā tas-harū
sentences.l: Then Sharrukān said to them: You fought today and grew tired from the fighting, so it is fitting that you go to your places and sleep and do not stay-awake.
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān said to them, “You have fought today and are tired from the battle. You should go to your quarters and sleep, and not sit up.”

sentences.t: فَأَجَابُوهُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ وَتَوَجَّهَ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمْ إِلَى سُرَادِقِهِ وَمَابَقِيَ عِنْدَ شَرْكَانَ سِوَى قَلِيلٍ مِنَ الْغِلْمَانِ وَالْعَجُوزِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: fa-ajābūhu ilā dhālika wa-tawajjaha kullun minhum ilā surādiqihi wa-mā baqiya ʿinda sharrukāna siwā qalīlin mina al-ghilmāni wa-al-ʿajūzi dhāti al-dawāhī
sentences.l: And they answered him to that, and each one of them went to his pavilion, and there did not remain with Sharrukān other than a few of the pages and the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī.
sentences.i: They agreed to this, and each of them went off to his pavilion, and no one was left with Sharrukān but a few of his pages and the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī.
sentences.n: ajāba ilā: “consent to (a request)”. ومابقي is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَتَحَدَّثَ مَعَهَا قَلِيلً مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ اضْطَجَعَ لِيَنَامَ وَكَذَلِكَ الْغِلْمَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-taḥaddatha maʿahā qalīlan mina al-layli thumma iḍṭajaʿa li-yanāma wa-ka-dhālika al-ghilmānu
sentences.l: And he talked with her a little of the night, then lay down to sleep, and likewise the pages.
sentences.i: He talked with her for a little of the night, then lay down to sleep, and so did the pages.
sentences.n: Classical Arabic writes the accusative qalīlan with a final alif (قليلا); the print has قليل without it, a common Middle Arabic spelling, and the pointing reads it as the adverb the sense needs.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ غَلَبَ عَلَيْهِمُ النَّوْمُ فَصَارُوا مِثْلَ الْأَمْوَاتِ
sentences.tr: thumma ghalaba ʿalayhimu al-nawmu fa-ṣārū mithla al-amwāti
sentences.l: Then the sleep overcame them, and they became like the dead.
sentences.i: Then sleep overcame them, and they lay like the dead.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ شَرْكَانَ وَغِلْمَانِهِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri sharrukāna wa-ghilmānihi
sentences.l: This is what was of the affair of Sharrukān and his pages.
sentences.i: So much for Sharrukān and his pages.
sentences.n: The storyteller’s formula for leaving one thread and taking up another; its partner, wa-ammā mā kāna min amri …, “and as for the affair of …”, follows at once.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْعَجُوزِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي فَإِنَّهَا بَعْدَ نَوْمِهِمْ صَارَتْ يَقْظَانَةً وَحْدَهَا فِى الْخَيْمَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-ʿajūzi dhāti al-dawāhī fa-innahā baʿda nawmihim ṣārat yaqẓānatan waḥdahā fī al-khaymati
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, she, after their sleep, became awake, alone in the tent.
sentences.i: As for the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī: once they were asleep, she was the only one awake in the tent.
sentences.n: yaqẓāna, “awake” (fem.), is a non-Classical feminine of yaqẓān; Classical Arabic says yaqẓā.

sentences.t: وَنَظَرَتْ إِلَى شَرْكَانَ فَوَجَدَتْهُ مُسْتَغْرِقًا فِى النَّوْمِ
sentences.tr: wa-naẓarat ilā sharrukāna fa-wajadathu mustaghriqan fī al-nawmi
sentences.l: And she looked at Sharrukān and found him sunk in the sleep.
sentences.i: She looked at Sharrukān and found him sunk in sleep.

sentences.t: فَوَثَبَتْ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهَا كَأَنَّهَا دُبَّةٌ مَعْطَا أَوْ آفَةٌ رَقْطَا
sentences.tr: fa-wathabat ʿalā qadamayhā ka-annahā dubbatun maʿṭā aw āfatun raqṭā
sentences.l: And she leapt onto her two feet as if she were a hairless she-bear or a speckled bane.
sentences.i: She sprang to her feet like a mangy she-bear or a speckled pest.
sentences.n: A rhymed simile (maʿṭā / raqṭā, for Classical maʿṭāʾ, raqṭāʾ, the final hamza dropped as the print often drops it). The marks on دُبّة are the print’s. āfa means a blight or bane; the simile may first have had افعى (afʿā, “viper”), whose stock epithet is raqṭāʾ, “speckled”; but the print’s word makes sense and is kept.

sentences.t: وَأَخْرَجَتْ مِنْ وَسَطِهَا خَنْجَرًا مَسْمُومًا لَوْ وُضِعَ عَلَى صَخْرَةٍ لَأَذَابَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-akhrajat min wasaṭihā khanjaran masmūman law wuḍiʿa ʿalā ṣakhratin la-adhābahā
sentences.l: And she brought out from her middle a poisoned dagger: if it were placed on a rock, it would have melted it.
sentences.i: From her waist she drew a poisoned dagger that would have melted a rock if it were laid on one.
sentences.n: la-adhābahā: the la- that answers a law “if” clause. The fatḥa on that lām is the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَرَّدَتْهُ مِنْ غِمْدِهِ وَأَتَتْ عِنْدَ رَأْسِ شَرْكَانَ وَجَرَّتْهُ عَلَى رَقَبَتِهِ فَذَبَحَتْهُ وَأَزَالَتْ رَأْسَهُ عَنْ جَسَدِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma jarradathu min ghimdihi wa-atat ʿinda raʾsi sharrukāna wa-jarrathu ʿalā raqabatihi fa-dhabaḥathu wa-azālat raʾsahu ʿan jasadihi
sentences.l: Then she bared it from its sheath and came to the head of Sharrukān, and drew it across his neck, and slaughtered him, and removed his head from his body.
sentences.i: Then she drew it from its sheath, came to Sharrukān’s head, drew it across his throat and cut it, and took his head off his body.
sentences.n: jarradathu / jarrathu: “she unsheathed it” and “she drew it”, two verbs a letter apart.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَثَبَتْ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهَا وَأَتَتْ إِلَى الْغِلْمَانِ النِّيَامِ وَقَطَعَتْ رُؤُسَهُمْ لِئَلَّا يَنْتَبِهُوا
sentences.tr: thumma wathabat ʿalā qadamayhā wa-atat ilā al-ghilmāni al-niyāmi wa-qaṭaʿat ruʾūsahum li-allā yantabihū
sentences.l: Then she leapt onto her feet and came to the sleeping pages and cut off their heads, lest they wake.
sentences.i: Then she sprang up, went to the sleeping pages and cut off their heads so that they would not wake.
sentences.n: The print spells ruʾūs “heads” رؤس, with one wāw; Classical spelling has رؤوس.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجَتْ مِنَ الْخَيْمَةِ وَأَتَتْ إِلَى خِيَامِ السُّلْطَانِ فَوَجَدَتِ الْحُرَّاسَ غَيْرَ نَائِمِينَ
sentences.tr: thumma kharajat mina al-khaymati wa-atat ilā khiyāmi al-sulṭāni fa-wajadati al-ḥurrāsa ghayra nāʾimīna
sentences.l: Then she went out from the tent and came to the tents of the sultan, and found the guards not sleeping.
sentences.i: Then she left the tent and went to the sultan’s tents, but found the guards awake.
sentences.n: The shadda on الحرّاس is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَمَالَتْ إِلَى خَيْمَةِ الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ فَوَجَدَتْهُ يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ
sentences.tr: fa-mālat ilā khaymati al-wazīri dandāna fa-wajadathu yaqraʾu al-qurʾāna
sentences.l: And she turned aside to the tent of the vizier Dandān, and found him reading the Qurʾān.
sentences.i: So she turned aside to the vizier Dandān’s tent, and found him reciting the Qurʾān.

sentences.t: فَوَقَعَتْ عَيْنُهُ عَلَيْهَا فَقَالَ مَرْحَبًا بِالزَّاهِدِ الْعَابِدِ
sentences.tr: fa-waqaʿat ʿaynuhu ʿalayhā fa-qāla marḥaban bi-al-zāhidi al-ʿābidi
sentences.l: And his eye fell on her, and he said: Welcome to the ascetic, the worshipper!
sentences.i: His eye fell on her, and he said, “Welcome, devout and holy man!”
sentences.n: marḥaban bi-: “welcome to”; the bi- marks the one greeted.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْوَزِيرِ ارْتَجَفَ قَلْبُهَا وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّ سَبَبَ مَجِيئِي إِلَى هُنَا فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ أَنِّي سَمِعْتُ صَوْتَ وَلِيٍّ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاوِ اللَّهِ وَأَنَا ذَاهِبٌ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat dhālika mina al-wazīri irtajafa qalbuhā wa-qālat lahu inna sababa majīʾī ilā hunā fī hādhā al-waqti annī samiʿtu ṣawta waliyyin min awliyāwi allāhi wa-anā dhāhibun ilayhi
sentences.l: And when she heard that from the vizier, her heart trembled, and she said to him: The cause of my coming to here at this time is that I heard the voice of a friend from the friends of God, and I am going to him.
sentences.i: When she heard this from the vizier her heart shook, and she said to him, “I have come here at this hour because I heard the voice of one of God’s saints, and I am on my way to him.”
sentences.n: walī Allāh, “friend of God”: a saint. The print spells the plural اولياو, with a wāw for the hamza of awliyāʾ, a Middle Arabic spelling. In her disguise she speaks of herself in the masculine (dhāhib, “going”).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَلَّتْ
sentences.tr: thumma wallat
sentences.l: Then she turned away.
sentences.i: Then she turned and went.
sentences.n: The shadda on ولّت is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَاللَّهِ لَأَ تْبَعُ هَذَا الزَّاهِدَ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru dandānu fī nafsihi wa-allāhi la-atbaʿu hādhā al-zāhida fī hādhihi al-laylati
sentences.l: And the vizier Dandān said in himself: By God, I will surely follow this ascetic in this night.
sentences.i: The vizier Dandān said to himself, “By God, I will follow this holy man tonight.”
sentences.n: The print divides the verb wrongly, لا تبع, which as it stands would read “do not follow”. The sense, and what Dandān does next, ask for la-atbaʿu (لاتبع), “I will surely follow”: the oath’s la- on atbaʿu. The space is kept where the print sets it, and the pointing reads across it.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ وَمَشَى خَلْفَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma wa-mashā khalfahā
sentences.l: And he rose and walked behind her.
sentences.i: He got up and walked after her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَحَسَّتِ الْمَلْعُونَةُ بِمَشْيِهِ عَرَفَتْ أَنَّهُ وَرَاءَهَا فَخَشِيَتْ أَنْ تَفْتَضِحَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aḥassati al-malʿūnatu bi-mashyihi ʿarafat annahu warāʾahā fa-khashiyat an taftaḍiḥa
sentences.l: And when the accursed woman sensed his walking, she knew that he was behind her, and she feared that she would be exposed.
sentences.i: When the accursed woman heard his steps, she knew he was behind her and was afraid she would be found out.
sentences.n: aḥassa bi-: “perceive, become aware of”; the verb takes bi-.

sentences.t: وَقَٰلَتْ فِي نَفْسِهَا إِنْ لَمْ أَخْدَعْهُ بِحِيلَةٍ فَإِنِّي أَفْتَضِحُ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat fī nafsihā in lam akhdaʿhu bi-ḥīlatin fa-innī aftaḍiḥu maʿahu
sentences.l: And she said in herself: If I do not trick him with a ruse, I shall be exposed with him.
sentences.i: She said to herself, “If I do not trick him somehow, he will see through me.”
sentences.n: The print spells qālat “she said” قلت, without its long ā (the dagger alif supplies it), as it sometimes does with this verb.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَتْ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ بَعِيدٍ وَقَالَتْ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ إِنِّي سَائِرٌ خَلْفَ هَذَا الْوَلِيِّ لِأَعْرِفَهُ وَبَعْدَ أَنْ أَعْرِفَهُ أَسْتَأْذِنُهُ فِي مَجِيئِكَ إِلَيْهِ وَأُقْبِلُ عَلَيْكَ وَأُخْبِرُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbalat ilayhi min baʿīdin wa-qālat ayyuhā al-wazīru innī sāʾirun khalfa hādhā al-waliyyi li-aʿrifahu wa-baʿda an aʿrifahu astaʾdhinuhu fī majīʾika ilayhi wa-uqbilu ʿalayka wa-ukhbiruka
sentences.l: And she came toward him from far, and said: O vizier, I am going behind this friend-of-God to know him, and after I know him I ask-his-leave for your coming to him, and I come to you and inform you.
sentences.i: So she came back toward him from a distance and said, “Vizier, I am following this saint to find out who he is. Once I know him, I will ask his leave for you to come to him, and come back to you and tell you.
sentences.n: li-aʿrifahu: li- of purpose, “in order to know him”. istaʾdhana fī: “ask permission for”.

sentences.t: لِأَنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ مَعِي بِغَيْرِ اسْتِئْذَانِ الْوَلِيِّ فَيَحْصُلَ لَهُ نَفْرَةٌ مِنِّي إِذَا رَآكَ مَعِي
sentences.tr: li-annī akhāfu an tadhhaba maʿī bi-ghayri istiʾdhāni al-waliyyi fa-yaḥṣula lahu nafratun minnī idhā raʾāka maʿī
sentences.l: Because I fear that you go with me without the asking-leave of the friend-of-God, and there comes-about for him an aversion from me if he sees you with me.
sentences.i: For I am afraid that if you come with me without the saint’s leave, he will take against me when he sees you with me.”
sentences.n: The shadda on لانّي is the print’s. yaḥṣulu, a masculine verb before a feminine subject (nafra, “aversion”), is a common loose agreement when the verb comes first.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ كَلَامَهَا اسْتَحَى أَنْ يَرُدَّ عَلَيْهَا جَوَابًا فَتَرَكَهَا وَرَجَعَ إِلَى خَيْمَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru kalāmahā istaḥā an yarudda ʿalayhā jawāban fa-tarakahā wa-rajaʿa ilā khaymatihi
sentences.l: And when the vizier heard her speech, he was ashamed to return to her an answer, and he left her and returned to his tent.
sentences.i: When the vizier heard this he was too embarrassed to answer back, so he let her go and went back to his tent.
sentences.n: istaḥā is a short form of istaḥyā, “be ashamed, shrink from”. The shadda on يردّ is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَأَرَادَأَنْ يَنَامَ فَمَا طَابَ لَهُ مَنَامٌ وَكَادَتِ الدُّنْيَا أَنْ تَنْطَبِقَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-arāda an yanāma fa-mā ṭāba lahu manāmun wa-kādati al-dunyā an tanṭabiqa ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And he wanted to sleep, and sleep was not sweet for him, and the world almost closed upon him.
sentences.i: He tried to sleep, but sleep would not come, and the world seemed to be closing in on him.
sentences.n: واردان is printed as one word (wa-arāda an), and kept so.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ وَخَرَجَ مِنْ خَيْمَتِهِ وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ أَنَا أَمْضِي إِلَى شَرْكَانَ وَأَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَهُ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma wa-kharaja min khaymatihi wa-qāla fī nafsihi anā amḍī ilā sharrukāna wa-ataḥaddathu maʿahu ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And he rose and went out from his tent and said in himself: I go to Sharrukān and talk with him until the morning.
sentences.i: He got up, went out of his tent, and said to himself, “I will go to Sharrukān and talk with him till morning.”

sentences.t: فَسَارَ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلَ خَيْمَةَ شَرْكَانَ فَوَجَدَ الدَّمَ سَائِلًا كَالْقَنَاةِ وَنَظَرَ الْغِلْمَانَ مَذْبُوحِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-sāra ilā an dakhala khaymata sharrukāna fa-wajada al-dama sāʾilan ka-al-qanāti wa-naẓara al-ghilmāna madhbūḥīna
sentences.l: And he went until he entered the tent of Sharrukān, and found the blood flowing like the channel, and saw the pages slaughtered.
sentences.i: He walked on until he came into Sharrukān’s tent, and found the blood running like a stream, and saw the pages with their throats cut.
sentences.n: ka-: “like” (prep.). naẓara here takes a direct object, “saw”, without the usual ilā.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَ صَيْحَةً أَزْعَجَتْ مَنْ كَانَ نَائِمًا فَتَسَارَعَتِ الْخَلْقُ إِلَيْهِ فَرَأَوُا الدَّمَ سَائِلًا فَضَجُّوا بِالْبُكَاءِ وَالنَّحِيبِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥa ṣayḥatan azʿajat man kāna nāʾiman fa-tasāraʿati al-khalqu ilayhi fa-raʾawu al-dama sāʾilan fa-ḍajjū bi-al-bukāʾi wa-al-naḥībi
sentences.l: And he cried a cry that disturbed whoever was sleeping, and the people hurried to him and saw the blood flowing, and they clamoured with the weeping and the wailing.
sentences.i: He let out a cry that woke whoever was asleep, and people came running, saw the blood flowing, and broke into loud weeping and wailing.
sentences.n: al-khalq, “the creatures, the people”, is a collective, and the verb treats it as feminine (tasāraʿat). ḍajja bi-: “raise a clamour of”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ اسْتَيْقَظَ السُّلْطَانُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَسَأَلَ عَنِ الْخَبَرِ فَقِيلَ لَهُ إِنَّ شَرْكَانَ أَخَاكَ وَالْغِلْمَانَ مَقْتُولُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika istayqaẓa al-sulṭānu ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-saʾala ʿani al-khabari fa-qīla lahu inna sharrukāna akhāka wa-al-ghilmāna maqtūlūna
sentences.l: And at that the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān woke and asked about the news, and it was said to him: Sharrukān your brother and the pages are killed.
sentences.i: At this the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān woke and asked what had happened, and was told, “Your brother Sharrukān and the pages have been killed.”
sentences.n: akhāka, “your brother”, stands in apposition to Sharrukān, which inna makes accusative, so the accusative is regular here; the plural predicate maqtūlūna covers Sharrukān and the pages together.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ مُسْرِعًا إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلَ الْخَيْمَةَ فَوَجَدَ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ يَصِيحُ وَوَجَدَ جُثَّةَ أَخِيهِ بِلَا رَأْسٍ فَغَابَ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma musriʿan ilā an dakhala al-khaymata fa-wajada al-wazīra dandāna yaṣīḥu wa-wajada juththata akhīhi bi-lā raʾsin fa-ghāba ʿani al-dunyā
sentences.l: And he rose hastening until he entered the tent, and found the vizier Dandān crying out, and found the corpse of his brother without a head; and he went absent from the world.
sentences.i: He got up and hurried until he came into the tent, and found the vizier Dandān crying out, and his brother’s body without its head; and he fainted away.
sentences.n: ghāba ʿan al-dunyā, “he went absent from the world”: he fainted.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَتْ كُلُّ الْعَسَاكِرِ وَبَكَوْا وَدَارُوا حَوْلَ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ سَاعَةً حَتَّى اسْتَفَاقَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥat kullu al-ʿasākiri wa-bakaw wa-dārū ḥawla ḍawʾi al-makāni sāʿatan ḥattā istafāqa
sentences.l: And all the troops cried out and wept, and went around Ḍawʾ al-Makān an hour, until he recovered.
sentences.i: The whole army cried out and wept, and they stood round Ḍawʾ al-Makān a while until he came to himself.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ إِلَى شَرْكَانَ وَبَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَفَعَلَ مِثْلَهُ الْوَزِيرُ وَرُسْتُمُ وَبَهْرَامُ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓara ilā sharrukāna wa-bakā bukāʾan shadīdan wa-faʿala mithlahu al-wazīru wa-rustumu wa-bahrāmu
sentences.l: Then he looked at Sharrukān and wept a strong weeping, and the vizier and Rustam and Bahrām did the like of him.
sentences.i: Then he looked at Sharrukān and wept bitterly, and so did the vizier, Rustam and Bahrām.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْحَاجِبُ فَإِنَّهُ صَاحَ وَأَكْثَرَ مِنَ النُّوَاحِ ثُمَّ طَلَبَ الِارْتِحَالَ لِمَابِهِ مِنَ الْأَوْجَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-ḥājibu fa-innahu ṣāḥa wa-akthara mina al-nuwāḥi thumma ṭalaba al-irtiḥāla li-mā bihi mina al-awjāli
sentences.l: And as for the chamberlain, he cried out and made-much of the lamenting; then he sought the departing, for what was in him of the fears.
sentences.i: The chamberlain cried out and lamented long and loud, and then asked to break camp, so frightened was he.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-nuwāḥ / al-irtiḥāl / al-awjāl. لمابه is printed as one word (li-mā bihi, “because of what was in him”).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ أَمَا عَلِمْتُمْ بِالَّذِى فَعَلَ بِأَخِي هَذِهِ الْفِعَالَ وَمَالِي لَا أَرَى الزَّاهِدَ الَّذِي عَنْ مَتَاعِ الدُّنْيَا مُتَبَاعِدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku a-mā ʿalimtum bi-alladhī faʿala bi-akhī hādhihi al-fiʿāla wa-mā lī lā arā al-zāhida alladhī ʿan matāʿi al-dunyā mutabāʿidun
sentences.l: And the king said: Do you not know of the one who did to my brother these deeds? And what is to me that I do not see the ascetic who from the goods of the world is far-removed?
sentences.i: The king said, “Do you not know who did these things to my brother? And why do I not see the holy man who keeps himself far from the goods of this world?”
sentences.n: ʿalima bi-: “know of”; faʿala bi-: “do (something) to”. wa-mā lī lā arā: “and what is the matter with me that I do not see”, an idiom for “why don’t I see”. The rhyme pairs al-zāhid with mutabāʿid.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ وَمَنْ جَلَبَ هَذِهِ الْأَحْزَانَ إِلَّا هَذَا الزَّاهِدُ الشَّيْطَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru wa-man jalaba hādhihi al-aḥzāna illā hādhā al-zāhidu al-shayṭānu
sentences.l: And the vizier said: And who brought these sorrows except this ascetic, the devil?
sentences.i: The vizier said, “Who has brought these sorrows on us but this devil of an ascetic?
sentences.n: The shadda on الّا is the print’s. al-aḥzān rhymes with al-shayṭān.

sentences.t: فَوَاللَّهِ إِنَّ قَلْبِي نَفَرَ مِنْهُ فِى الْأَوَّلِ وَالْآخِرِ لِأَنَّنِي أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ كُلَّ مُتَنَطِّعٍ فِى الدِّينِ خَبِيثٌ مَاكِرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-wa-allāhi inna qalbī nafara minhu fī al-awwali wa-al-ākhiri li-annanī aʿrifu anna kulla mutanaṭṭiʿin fī al-dīni khabīthun mākirun
sentences.l: For by God, my heart shied from him in the first and the last, because I know that every one going-to-extremes in the religion is vile, cunning.
sentences.i: By God, my heart shrank from him from first to last, for I know that everyone who makes a show of excess in religion is a wicked deceiver.”
sentences.n: mutanaṭṭiʿ: one who goes to extremes, who overdoes piety for show.

sentences.t: وَأَعَادَ عَلَي الْمَلِكِ قِصَّتَهُ وَأَنَّهُ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَتْبَعَهُ فَمَا مَكَّنَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿāda ʿalā al-maliki qiṣṣatahu wa-annahu arāda an yatbaʿahu fa-mā makkanahu
sentences.l: And he repeated to the king his story, and that he wanted to follow him, and he did not allow him.
sentences.i: He told the king again what had happened to him, how he had wanted to follow the ascetic and the ascetic would not let him.
sentences.n: The print spells ʿalā “to” with a dotted yā (علي) here. aʿāda ʿalā, “repeat to”. The shadda on مكّنه is the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ النَّاسَ ضَجُّوا بِالْبُكَاءِ وَالنَّحِيبِ وَتَضَرَّعُوا إِلَى الْقَرِيبِ الْمُجِيبِ أَنْ يُوقِعَ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ ذَلِكَ الزَّاهِدَ الَّذِي هُوَ لِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ جَاحِدٌ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-nāsa ḍajjū bi-al-bukāʾi wa-al-naḥībi wa-taḍarraʿū ilā al-qarībi al-mujībi an yūqiʿa bayna aydīhim dhālika al-zāhida alladhī huwa li-āyāti allāhi jāḥidun
sentences.l: Then the people clamoured with the weeping and the wailing, and humbly-implored the Near, the Answering, that He make-fall between their hands that ascetic who is a denier of the signs of God.
sentences.i: Then the people raised a clamour of weeping and wailing, and humbly begged the Near, the One who answers prayer, to deliver into their hands that ascetic who denies the signs of God.
sentences.n: al-Qarīb, “the Near”, and al-Mujīb, “the One who answers”, are names of God (Qurʾān 11:61), and rhyme here with al-naḥīb. li-āyāti allāhi jāḥid: jaḥada normally takes its object directly or with bi-; here the object is put before the participle jāḥid, and li- marks it. The shaddas on ضجّوا and تضرّعوا are the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَهَّزُوا شَرْكَانَ وَدَفَنُوهُ فِى الْجَبَلِ الْمَذْكُورِ وَحَزِنُوا عَلَى فَضْلِهِ الْمَشْهُورِ
sentences.tr: thumma jahhazū sharrukāna wa-dafanūhu fī al-jabali al-madhkūri wa-ḥazinū ʿalā faḍlihi al-mashhūri
sentences.l: Then they prepared Sharrukān, and buried him in the mountain mentioned, and grieved over his famed excellence.
sentences.i: Then they laid out Sharrukān and buried him on the mountain already spoken of, and mourned his famous virtue.
sentences.n: jahhaza: “prepare (a body) for burial”. “The mountain mentioned” is one spoken of earlier in the tale. The rhyme falls on al-madhkūr / al-mashhūr.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
